---
title: "07 · ANOVA as a linear model"
subtitle: "Week 2"
---

::: {.guiding-q}
And what about ANOVA?
:::

## In this session

- One-way ANOVA = linear model with one categorical predictor (session 04 revisited)
- Factorial ANOVA = categorical predictors with interactions (session 05 revisited)
- *F*-tests as comparisons between nested models
- Types of sums of squares (I, II, III) and why the order of terms can matter
- Repeated measures: a first look at non-independence (prepares session 11)

::: {.key-terms}
**Key terms:** [Contrasts and dummy coding](../../glossary.qmd#contrasts), [Degrees of freedom](../../glossary.qmd#df)
:::

## Learning goals

After this session you can

- reproduce an ANOVA table from a linear model,
- explain an *F*-test as a comparison of a full and a reduced model,
- choose an appropriate type of sums of squares for unbalanced data.

## Simulate first

```{r}
set.seed(7)
group <- factor(rep(c("control", "food", "toy"), each = 20))
y     <- rnorm(60, c(control = 10, food = 14, toy = 12)[group], 3)

summary(aov(y ~ group))            # classic one-way ANOVA

full <- lm(y ~ group)
null <- lm(y ~ 1)
anova(null, full)                  # same F: a comparison of two models
```
